subject: Compartmented network proof + CAIQ mapping for Dedicated / Private
messages:
From: Acme Security <security-requests@acme-corp.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: CAIQ mapping + minimal network proof for Dedicated/Private

Hi Logan,

We are working through the procurement security checklist for Veridian Bank and need a compact, machine-readable CAIQ mapping plus a brief network "proof" that demonstrates how Redwood compartmentalizes tenant traffic for Dedicated and Private offerings. Specifically we need: 

- One-page CAIQ-sourced mapping that points to controls and artifacts (SOC2 sections, SIG rows, CAIQ IDs).
- A concise network sketch (PNG or PDF) showing Dedicated GPU pools, control-plane isolation, and the path an inference request takes (ingress -> runtime -> KV cache -> egress), annotated for trust boundaries.
- A short list of verification artifacts (logs, test steps) that we can hand to our internal auditors.

Can you provide this by COB Thursday (2027-09-16)? If not, please give an earliest-delivery ETA and the minimal deliverable we can accept for now.

Thanks,
Jae (on behalf of Veridian procurement)
Jae Park
Security Sourcing | Veridian Bank

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Acme Security <security-requests@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ mapping + minimal network proof for Dedicated/Private

Hi Jae,

Thanks — we can do a compact deliverable that meets your auditor's needs. High-level plan: 

1) Deliverable A (by EOD 2027-09-13): 
   - one-page CAIQ->Redwood control mapping (PDF) that references SOC 2 sections + SIG rows, and links to artifacts.
   - a single-page network sketch (PNG) with annotated trust boundaries and callouts for runtime, KV cache, and egress controls (attached: compartmented-network-mini-diagram.png).

2) Deliverable B (by 2027-09-16): 
   - artifacts bundle: curated log extracts (segmentation-verification.log), a short runbook for verification steps, and a signed assertion if required.

Quick notes on scope:
- This will cover Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem) high-level flows — not every customer's bespoke routing.
- Where controls differ (e.g., customer-managed KMS in Private), the mapping will show the control variation rather than replicate full architecture.

Im looping Kimberley and Soojin to confirm the verification log slices and to add any additional controls content for CAIQ mapping. If you can share an auditor email or specifics on the CAIQ checklist rows that Veridian cares most about, well prioritize those.

Regards,

Logan Wright
Manager, Security Programs 
Redwood Inference

Attachment: compartmented-network-mini-diagram.png (PNG, 1.2MB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-11T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ mapping + minimal network proof for Dedicated/Private

Logan / Soojin —

Drafted the CAIQ mapping summary and pulled the verification artifacts. Key points to surface in the one-pager: 

- Tenant separation model: Dedicated uses tenant-dedicated GPU pools + network ACLs per pool; Private uses VPC with customer-managed routing and optional on-prem gateway. Both use control-plane-authenticated APIs over mTLS to prevent control-plane injection.

- Data path classification: request metadata + KV cache keys are logically scoped per-tenant. For Dedicated we apply hypervisor-level namespace isolation where applicable and application-level tenancy checks in the inference runtime. For Private, data flow is contained by the customer's VPC routing plus overlay ACLs.

- Controls mapping highlights: 
  * CAIQ: NET-4 network isolation -> reference to segmented control-plane subnets, firewall policies (artifact: segmentation-verification.log)
  * CAIQ: CRY-2 KMS integration (Private) -> reference to KMS wiring doc (will link)
  * CAIQ: LOG-1 audit logging -> link to log retention policy + example log slice

Verification artifacts attached: segmentation-verification.log (redacted), and a short runbook we used during internal verification. I also annotated the PNG to show the control-plane egress lock (note callout #3).

I recommend the one-pager explicitly say: "This summary is evidence-backed and suitable for initial auditor review. For SOC 2-level attestations, submit the artifacts bundle (Deliverable B)."

+1 on the delivery dates.

-Kim

Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: segmentation-verification.log (text excerpt, redacted)

From: Acme Security <security-requests@acme-corp.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Jae Park <jae.park@veridianbank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ mapping + minimal network proof for Dedicated/Private

Hi Logan / Kim,

Thanks — this looks good for an initial pass. Two asks before we route to Veridian auditors: 

1) Can you embed an explicit statement of scope on the one-pager that lists what is *not* covered (examples: customer-managed peering specifics, on-prem edge configurations)?
2) Veridian procurement needs a short sign-off (simple signature or DocuSign) that the artifacts provided are accurate to the best of Redwoods knowledge. Can you route a DocuSign for the assertion?

If those are doable, we can get this to the auditors by Monday. Sending a DocuSign link would be easiest.

Jae

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Logan
